9 February 2026

Artificial Intelligence

The Self-Forging Mind: A Framework That Builds Its Own Training Ground

RLAnything dynamically forges its own environment, policy, and reward models in a closed loop—reshaping how AI agents learn.

Researchers at the intersection of reinforcement learning and large language models have introduced RLAnything, a framework that reimagines how AI agents acquire skill. Rather than training against a fixed environment, the system simultaneously optimizes the environment, the policy, and the reward model in a continuous closed loop.

The system integrates step-wise action feedback with final-outcome signals to train the policy, while a jointly optimized reward model amplifies learning through consistency feedback. The results are striking: a 9.1% boost on OSWorld, an 18.7% gain on AlfWorld, and 11.9% on LiveBench. Most telling, the optimized reward-model signals outperformed outcomes relying solely on human labels—suggesting a path toward more autonomous, self-improving AI systems.

Source: Wang, Xie, Shen, Wang & Yang — RLAnything (2026)

Key Insight Optimized reward-model signals outperformed outcomes relying solely on human labels—marking a step toward AI training that needs less human scaffolding.

02 · Healthcare & Drug Discovery

DrugR: Teaching Molecules to Reason

Where prior LLM tools treat the structure-to-property relationship as an opaque black box, DrugR forces the model to articulate its pharmacological reasoning at each step. The framework integrates domain-specific continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning via reverse data engineering, and self-balanced multi-granular reinforcement learning to improve key ADMET properties—absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity—of candidate molecules.

By making the reasoning process explicit rather than implicit, the researchers aim to provide more reliable, interpretable pathways for identifying viable drug candidates—a meaningful step toward trustworthy AI-assisted drug discovery.

Source: Liu, Zeng, Yan, Chen & Xiao — DrugR (arXiv, February 2026)
